lesson_title: Theory Paper Practice Run: Walking Structured Questions at Exam Pace
hook_text: Eight marks. Four sentences. One recipe that answers every paragraph question Geography can throw at you.
clip_script: Paragraph tasks decide strong finishes, so the run closes there. The contract: eight marks as four ideas at two marks each, in full sentences, pitched where thinking is required. The recipe has four moves. Read the instruction verb and obey it — suggest wants workable solutions, evaluate wants a judgement backed by evidence. Plan four ideas in the margin as four keywords before writing any prose. Write one sentence per idea and develop each one — the second mark of every pair is earned by the because-clause. And keep the topic's own vocabulary on the page: a paragraph about drought that never says food security or irrigation leaves vocabulary marks unclaimed. Four keywords, four sentences, eight marks — the identical recipe answers every paragraph task the subject can offer.
visual_style: Practice page mock-up filling itself in: a margin sprouting four keywords, then four sentences typing out one by one, each stamping +2 as its because-clause lands, ending on 8/8 circled in green.
mood: Locked-in exam training, calm and tactical.
pacing: Four crisp beats for the four moves, accelerating stamps of +2, clean win at the close.
call_to_action: Watch the full practice run and walk every question type before your final exams do.
